newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures deepen losses after rally.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures deepen losses after rally.

text.p: Renewed African and Far East origin selling and speculative profit taking to Wednesday's sharp advance took London robusta coffee prices lower on Thursday.
"The market is running out of steam for the time being," said one trader. Coffee reaped some six percent gains on Wednesday on funds-led buying.
A lower start in New York also dragged the values down. The market had been hammered by day-long origin sales from Ivory Coast and Vietnam.
By the finish, benchmark March was $38 down at $1,532 a tonne. It had touched a low of $1,520.
Jan/March spread was active, trading at level money after a high of $75 on Wednesday as more coffee were graded and tendered ahead of January's expiry on Friday.
Traders said news Colombia would announce cuts in coffee exports next week had no impact.
Arabica-coffee producer nations agreed in Brazil last week to cut exports by 300,000 60-bags between January and June with top growers Brazil and Colombia likely to take a large slice in exports.

The market are also watching next week's talks in Indonesia among robusta producers on export quota allocations. Under the pact, robusta growers would have to trim exports by one million bags in the same period. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
